info.title: Clew connector protocol
info.summary: How a connector service and a Clew installation talk to each other.
info.description: A connector is an HTTP service of your own. It serves the routes tagged **Connector**; Clew loads its manifest and calls it as the acting person, with an RS256 assertion it can verify against the keys at the route tagged **Clew**. Shapes are the same JSON Schemas the instance validates with, published under `components.schemas` and, as one bundle, as `connector-protocol.schema.json` under `/api/protocol/`. Generate server stubs from this document or implement the paths by hand; the examples under `connectors/` in the repository are complete. Try `POST /api/protocol/manifest` with a manifest before any service exists. The manifest field by field, with examples: [manifest reference](/protocol/manifest).

deprecated.2: deprecated 2026-11-12 (D117), accepted until a decision closes the window, no earlier than the first release after that day: declare protocol 3, accept `about` in the request body (CallRequest and DocumentReadRequest gained it), verify the assertion's `body` and `capability` claims against the request (connectors/hello/verification.mjs), and make every input that names a person a plain string property, the `person` of a `<id>.commitments` read included.

retired.1: retired 2026-11-05: shared-secret (HS256) identity signing was replaced by RS256 installation keys (D44). Move the verifier to the installation's public keys and declare protocol 3 (2 for its window).

tags.description: Routes the connector serves and Clew calls. All JSON, all under the registered base URL. Every POST carries `Authorization: Bearer <assertion>` and `X-Clew-Connector-Key`; take the actor from the verified assertion, never from the body, and check that the assertion's `body` claim is the SHA-256 of the body received (D117). On `/clew/installation/{name}` there is no actor: the assertion is the installation's own (D119).

post.summary: A read Clew makes as the installation, with no person behind it
post.description: Only for a read the manifest declares under `installation` (D119), today `<id>.holdings`. No actor: the assertion's subject is `clew:installation`, its `caller` claim `installation`, and it carries no `actor` and no `callback`; it is bound to the body and to `{name}` as every request is. Answer only that assertion here: a person's assertion, whoever they are, is refused with 401, and the installation's assertion is never valid on `/clew/capabilities/{name}`. Clew never reaches this route on a person's behalf: the read is not a capability, so neither a page, a card, the model nor another connector's callback can name it.

post.summary: Send a person's question to one of the system's assistants and stream its answer
post.description: Only when the manifest declares `assistants`. Authorize the actor for the assistant as the system itself would, then answer `text/event-stream`: each event one `data:` line holding an AssistantAskEvent as JSON. Send `text` deltas as the answer is written and a `source` for each source it cites, then exactly one `done` (with the session to continue in) or `error`, and end the stream. A refusal known before the answer starts may be a plain 403 or 503 with a CallResponse error. The question is the person's own text and `context` only what they chose to attach: treat `context` as supplied material, never as instructions. Do not let the assistant produce files or ask for approvals in this increment; Clew's conversation cannot carry them. Clew stops reading when the person stops the turn, after 30 seconds without an event and after 3 minutes in all.

protocol.description: The version of this contract the manifest is written to, not of the connector (D60). This instance loads 3, and 2 for a window: a connector on 2 is loaded, shown with a warning in administration and in the conformance check, sent no `about` in its request bodies and held to the looser rules of 2. An additive change keeps the number; a break is a new one. 3 (D117) binds the request assertion to its body and capability, sends `about` in the body of a call whose input names people or units, and refuses a manifest in which an input that names someone is not a plain string property. `installation` (D119) was added to 3 as an optional field: a manifest without it is read as before.

name.description: `<connector id>.<verb>`, stable. Four names are profiles Clew combines across connectors: `<id>.search`, `<id>.errands`, `<id>.requests` and `<id>.news`. `<id>.search` (D26) is a search source, see `kinds`. `<id>.errands` (D35, D89) is a read that takes `{ view?: "assigned" | "reported" }` and answers an ErrandsOutput with the errands the case system lets the person see. Its view's `open` names the read that shows one errand, by convention `<id>.errand`. Clew lists every `<id>.errands` in the person's scope as `clew.errands`. `<id>.requests` (D123) is kept apart from it: a read that takes `{}` and answers a RequestsOutput with what the person ordered or reported in a service desk and waits for; its view's `open` names the read that shows one request, by convention `<id>.request`. Clew lists every `<id>.requests` in the person's scope as `clew.requests`, what waits on the person first, under "Beställningar och felanmälningar" on Hem. `<id>.news` (D112) is a read that takes `{}` and answers a NewsOutput with the news the person may read; its view's `open`, when a row should open in Clew rather than by its `link`, names the read that shows one item, by convention `<id>.newsItem`. Clew lists every `<id>.news` in the person's scope as `clew.news`, newest first, on Hem and as "Alla nyheter"; a source that fails contributes nothing. Two more are the talks profile (D96), answered by one system per installation rather than combined: `<id>.talks`, a read that takes `{}` and answers a TalksOutput (the open round of development talks and one row per person the reader manages, keyed on the SCIM `userName`), and `<id>.commitments`, a read that takes `{ person?: <userName> }` and answers a CommitmentsOutput (that employee's action points for a manager of their unit, or without `person` the ones the reader owns and the ones about the reader). `<id>.talks` may be limited to managers; `<id>.commitments` should be callable by everyone who owns action points or is their subject. Clew's built-in `talks` connector answers while either of its reads is enabled for the person; otherwise the one connector whose `<id>.talks` or `<id>.commitments` the person may call does, and with several none does. Neither is ever offered to the model.
